title: Eggplant Dip – Baba Ganoush
description: The key to this Eggplant Dip (Baba Ganoush) recipe is roasting the eggplant really well so it takes on a smoky flavor. Be sure to scrape every last bit of eggplant from the peel, the browned parts are what give the dip that deep smoky flavor. If you want a rustic eggplant dip, mix the ingredients well with a fork, if you want a more traditional creamy dip then blend the ingredients together with an immersion blender (hand-held blender) or in a blender. This dip is great on bread, warmed pitas, crostini or as a dip for vegetables.
ingredients: 1 large eggplant (about 600g), cut in half lengthwise
directions: Adjust oven rack 4 to 5 inches below the broiler and heat broiler.
Brush the cut sides of the eggplant with olive oil. Set the eggplant cut-side down on a foil-lined baking sheet.
Broil or roast in a very hot oven (450 degrees) until the eggplant halves are very wrinkled and very tender when pressed, about 40 minutes.
When cool enough to handle, use a big spoon and scrape the flesh from the eggplant into a colander, allowing it to sit for 3 minutes.
Blend or mix together roasted eggplant, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt and cumin.
Stir in fresh parsley and drizzle with a splash of olive oil (maybe some left in the roasting pan).
Have fun with this dip and make it your own! Try adding roasted garlic rather than raw. Mint rather than parsley. Add more lemon juice to give it more zing! Try garnishing with pomegranate seeds.

You can also grill the eggplants rather than roast them (on the outside grill or even the stovetop). Instead of slicing them lengthwise, leave them whole. Rotate over grill every 3-4 minutes until the flesh is very tender, blackened and wrinkled (collapsing in on itself), 12 to 15 minutes.

You can also finish that bowlful of smoky eggplant pulp by adding a long pour of fruity olive oil and seasoning it one of three ways: salt, microplaned raw garlic and lemon juice; tom yum paste and scallions and sesame seeds stirred in; or a heavy shower of freshly chopped parsley, some crumbled feta cheese and a little red onion.
